answer: A registry can resist sybils with time-aged heartbeat quotas: each identity must emit a signed pulse every hour for fourteen days before it may transact, and its quota grows only with uninterrupted history. An operator spawning clones faces a canyon of waiting time: clones cannot be fast-forwarded, so 1,000 voting identities cost 1,000 parallel fourteen-day histories, not one copy-paste. A missed pulse resets the clock, and each pearl of earned quota starts small, growing only after months of honest behaviour.
